subject: Telemetry export scrub & tracehook Qs for private deployment prep
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Ortiz <danielle.ortiz@globex.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Telemetry export scrub & tracehook Qs for private deployment prep

Danielle — thanks again for the kickoff this morning. As we prepare the private deployment handoff, a few specific telemetry questions from the engineering and security teams so we can lock design and acceptance tests. I put two small attachments (scrub rules draft + tracehook sample) — please review and let us know if any of these are blockers.

High-level ask: we want to confirm the agreed sanitization/PII redaction, auth and transport for SIEM ingest, and tracing hook sampling so our proof-of-transfer and audit evidence match Globex requirements. Concrete items: 
- SIEM ingest endpoint: will you accept Splunk HEC over mTLS, or do you require an in-VPC forwarder that terminates TLS internally? Any port restrictions?
- Token vs. mTLS: if both supported, what's your rotation cadence requirement for tokens/certs? Any HSM/KMS expectations?
- Required fields: are there mandatory fields/labels Globex needs on each event (customer_id, redwood_region, deployment_id, trace_id, span_id)? I attached a proposed minimal schema in the PDF.
- Scrub rules: high-level rules in the PDF — are these sufficient (PII: email, ssn, ipv4/6, authorization headers)? Any fields that must be retained unmasked for forensics?
- Tracing hooks: desired sampling rate and whether Globex will accept client-side sampling at 1% with tail-sampling in Splunk/OTEL, or if you require deterministic sampling for certain routes.

Proposed acceptance steps (tentative):
1) We push a short test bundle: 10k log events + 200 traces to your staging HEC (mTLS)
2) You verify schema and scrubbed fields and send a signed receipt (S3-styled metadata or HubSpot evidence)
3) We iterate any scrub exceptions and ship final config

Can we get answers to the bullet points above by EOD Monday so we can schedule the on-site run on Tuesday?

Attachments: 20260515-scrub-rules-draft.pdf, 20260515-tracehook-config-sample.yaml

Thanks — Mina
Mina Haddad

From: Danielle Ortiz <danielle.ortiz@globex.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: sec-ops@globex.com
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry export scrub & tracehook Qs for private deployment prep

Thanks Mina — good summary. Quick answers inline: 
- Ingest: we prefer Splunk HEC over mTLS from a vetted forwarder inside the customer VPC (we do not want public HEC endpoints across the internet). If you can run an internal forwarder (Fluentd/Fluent Bit or Splunk Connect) that terminates mTLS to our HEC cluster that’s ideal. Ports: 8088 outbound to our staging HEC IPs (we'll provide).
- Auth: mTLS preferred. For token-based HEC, tokens are acceptable for short-term testing only; production requires mTLS. Cert rotation: 90 days is our baseline for leaf certs, private CA cert rotation tracked in our audit. We can accept certs issued by your customer's internal PKI as long as we have the chain. No HSM requirement for transmission certs, but audit keys for long-term receipts should be in KMS.
- Required fields: you included most of them; please add event_origin (service name), event_level, env (staging/prod), and redwood_deployment_id. Trace fields (trace_id, span_id) must be present for every trace event we ingest.
- Scrub rules: the draft looks reasonable. Globex requirement: mask all full email addresses and replace with <EMAIL_REDACTED>, redact IPv4/6 except for /24 prefixes when necessary for network forensic indicators (we can accept truncated forms). Authorization headers must be stripped. Keep timestamps in RFC3339 UTC.
- Tracing: we accept client-side 1% sampling for general traffic, but require deterministic sampling for any requests that hit payment or PII-related routes (we will provide a small route list). Tail sampling on our end is OK as long as trace_id is preserved.

We'll send a staging HEC allowlist and a Confluence page with route list/requirements by EOD Monday. I can join the run Tuesday morning if needed.

— Danielle
Danielle Ortiz
Senior Security Engineer, Globex Corp.
danielle.ortiz@globex.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry export scrub & tracehook Qs for private deployment prep

On Fri, May 15, 2026 at 11:08 AM Danielle Ortiz <danielle.ortiz@globex.com> wrote:
> We'll send a staging HEC allowlist and a Confluence page with route list/requirements by EOD Monday. I can join the run Tuesday morning if needed.

Thanks — commenting with a short implementation pattern so Mina can include it in the runbook: 
- Forwarder pattern: deploy a lightweight forwarder in the customer's VPC (systemd container or daemonset): Fluent Bit -> local processing -> mTLS to Globex HEC. Reasons: lower blast radius, localized buffering, easier cert management.
- Scrubbing we will perform at the forwarder stage (Lua filter or regex stage in Fluent Bit) and again in the Redwood gateway as defense-in-depth. We'll implement the rules Danielle asked for: email -> <EMAIL_REDACTED>, strip Authorization headers, IPv4/6 truncation to /24 when flagged.
- Tracehooks: Redwood runtime will emit OTLP batch to the local forwarder in JSON/OTLP HTTP; forwarder will attach redwood_deployment_id and preserve trace_id/span_id. Proposed sampling config attached (tracehook-config-sample.yaml).
- Evidence receipts: after the test run, the forwarder will send a signed receipt (SHA256 manifest) to a Globex S3 bucket (pre-provisioned) and we'll include timestamped manifests in HBSP-48372.

Open items for the run:
1) Globex to provide staging HEC IPs and CA chain for mTLS.
2) Confirm which routes require deterministic tracing (Danielle said she'll share).
3) Confirm retention window for test data (we suggest 7 days in staging; prod retention per contract).

I'll stand up a quick k8s manifest + helm values we can bootstrap for the Tuesday run if we have IPs and CA.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal DevOps Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

- Globex: provide staging HEC IPs, CA chain, and deterministic-route list by EOD Monday (2026-05-18) — Danielle to own.
- Redwood: produce helm chart + Fluent Bit manifest, enable scrub rules (email/IP/authorization) and instrumentation to preserve trace_id/span_id — Jonas to own, PR by Tues 06:00 PT.
- Acceptance run: Tue 2026-05-19 09:00 PT — run bundle: ~10k events + 200 traces. Jonas will deploy forwarder to customer staging VPC; Danielle to validate schema & signed receipt.

I've attached a refreshed scrub rules PDF (same filename) with one small change: we will mask local-hostnames unless Globex requests them for debugging.
